newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crude grades fluctuate on volatile arb.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crude grades fluctuate on volatile arb.

text.p: U.S. cash crude outright prices gained strength to the end of Wednesday business, while domestic grades saw differentials fluctuate on a volatile Brent-West Texas Intermediate arbitrage.
August WTI/Cushing talked late Wednesday at $20.35-45 a barrel, around 25 cents stronger than late Tuesday clockings.
Cash grades dipped in the first half of the session, but sweet barrels -- notably Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James -- returned to favor later in the frame.

LLS sold at 17 and 18 cents over the August WTI/Cushing early, but ended at 20-23 cents above WTI, traders said. The earlier deals left LLS some five to six cents off yesterday levels, but late talk put the key sweet back to even.

The trans-Atlantic arbitrage moved out around 10 cents, raising expectations for more North Sea Brent crude shipments to the U.S. Gulf. August Brent-WTI spreads were close to $1.40, from $1.25-30 on Tuesday.
"That Brent-WTI has been all over the place, but the fact it ended up a dime wider has deflated some LLS momentum," said a cash dealer in Texas.
Other late grade talk had Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire around 25-30 cents cheaper than August WTI, with Midland/WTI steady from Tuesday at 30 cents below the marker.
For the sours, West Texas Sour/Midland ranged around a $1.00-10 discount all day, but later on the spread widened for bid and asks, out to a $1.15 discount, traders said.

Eugene Island barrels sold at a $1.32 disount, a few pennies weaker than Tuesday. August WTI/Cushing Postings Plus sold at $2.00, steady from Tuesday as the August/September WTI roll remained around flat to a few cents in favor of August.
